_: This repository's own declared quality gates — the checks it already runs, declared at their CURRENT measured values on 2026-09-15 (S20, the quality-ratchet slice; tightened to the new measured values on 2026-09-16, S22) so the ratchet starts where the repo is. Held by starter-kit/quality_ratchet.py --precommit, chained into .githooks/pre-commit: a commit that lowers any `min` below, raises any `max`, or removes a gate is refused; tightening and adding pass. Loosening is a plan-mode decision in its own commit with the reason in CHANGELOG.md, committed with --no-verify (SAFEGUARDS.md Blast Radius Limits). Measure with `python3 starter-kit/quality_ratchet.py --run` (about three minutes: it runs bin/tests.sh) and cite the summary line in the close-out receipt (HANDOFFS.md, runtime_smoke); bin/check-handoff lints for it.
_first_tightening_owed: DISCHARGED 2026-09-16 (S23, the first commit after PR #82 merged): `tests-sh-failed` tightened 1 -> 0 and `tests-sh-passed` 138 -> 139 once Test 9 turned green on main. Kept as the record of why the failed-count gate exists: a count gate is blind to health (a failing test still ran), so the FAILED count, held at 0, is what makes the suite's colour a gate. The next tightening is owed whenever a measured value rises: run --run, read the table, raise the floors — never lower them.
